name: Color picker
description: A control for choosing a color, either the native <input type="color"> or a panel with a color area, hue slider and value field. Use it when any color is allowed; for a few fixed colors, use a Radio group of swatches.
summary: Choose a color from a swatch or panel

elements.name: Label
elements.description: Visible <label> that names what the color is for

elements.name: Swatch
elements.description: Shows the current color and opens the picker

elements.name: Value field
elements.description: Text input for a hex or other color value

elements.name: Color area
elements.description: Two-dimensional area for saturation and brightness

elements.name: Hue slider
elements.description: Slider for hue; sometimes a second one for opacity

configOptions.options: Swatch only, Swatch and value field, Inline panel

variants.caption: Swatch and value field — compact row
variants.htmlOutline:
<label for="brand">Brand color</label>
<input id="brand" type="color" value="#2350d1">
<input aria-label="Brand color hex value" value="#2350d1" size="7">

variants.caption: Inline panel — color area, hue slider and value
variants.htmlOutline: Brand color

variants.caption: Presets — row of swatches with an add button
variants.htmlOutline:
<fieldset>
  <legend>Brand color</legend>
  <input type="radio" name="brand" value="#2350d1" aria-label="Blue" checked>
  <input type="radio" name="brand" value="#1a7f37" aria-label="Green">
  …
  <button type="button" aria-label="Add color">
    <svg aria-hidden="true">…</svg>
  </button>
</fieldset>

usageNotes: Start with the native <input type="color">. It opens the system picker, works with the keyboard, and always returns a hex value such as #2350d1.
Show the value as text next to the swatch, ideally in an editable field, so people can paste an exact color and the choice isn't shown by color alone (WCAG 1.4.1).
If only a few colors are allowed, such as product colors, use a Radio group styled as swatches and give each option a name ("Navy", not just a color).
A custom color area has no native role and needs dragging. Pair it with value fields or sliders built on the APG Slider pattern so the color can be set without dragging (WCAG 2.5.7).
